title: Lightbulb for Minister
statementMd:
The Minister for education is coming! Naturally, nobody wants to perform poorly in front of such a honored guest. However, two hours before the arrival it turned out that one of the classes has a malfunctioning lightbulb — for some reason it doesn't get enough energy. The solution was found quickly: all we've got to do is to change the location of the lightbulb so that it got the maximum amount of energy.

Everybody knows that the power of the lightbulb equals ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a90e7a205a459c09654686f74e0adc40b4c9f43a.png), where $*C*$ is some constant value and $*r*_{*i*}$ is the Euclidean distance from the bulb to the $*i*$-th generator. Consequently, our task is to minimize ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f797f28d86c195134fb9568607febdc9ad9f7336.png). Of course, we know the positions of all generators.

The bulb should be on the ceiling of the class. The ceiling of the class is in the form of a strictly convex $*m*$-gon (the class itself has the form of a right prism with a strictly convex $*m*$-gon at the bottom). Help to find the optimum location for the bulb. Assume that all generators are in the plane of the class ceiling. Consider that the plane of the class ceiling has some Cartesian coordinate system introduced.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ $(2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5})$ — the number of generators. Each of the next $*n*$ lines contains a pair of integers $*x*_{*i*}$, $*y*_{*i*}$, representing the coordinates of the $*i*$-th generator in the plane of the class ceiling. It's guaranteed that no two generators have the same location.

The next line contains integer $*m*$ $(3 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{5})$ — the number of vertexes in the convex polygon that describes the ceiling of the class. Each of the following $*m*$ lines contains a pair of integers $*p*_{*i*}, *q*_{*i*}$, representing the coordinates of the $*i*$-th point of the polygon in the clockwise order. It's guaranteed that the polygon is strictly convex.

The absolute value of all the coordinates don't exceed $10^{6}$.

## Output

Print a single real number — the minimum value of the sum of squares of distances from the generators to the point of the lightbulb's optimal position. The answer will be considered valid if its absolute or relative error doesn't exceed $10^{ - 4}$.

## Note

We'll define a strictly convex polygon as a convex polygon with the following property: no three vertices of the polygon lie on the same line.
statementZhMd:
教育部长要来了！当然，谁也不想在这样一位尊贵的客人面前表现糟糕。然而，在部长到来前两小时，我们发现其中一间教室的灯泡出了故障——不知为何，它没有获得足够的能量。解决方案很快就找到了：我们只需改变灯泡的位置，使其获得最大能量。

众所周知，灯泡的功率等于![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a90e7a205a459c09654686f74e0adc40b4c9f43a.png)，其中 $*C*$ 是某个常数，$*r*_{*i*}$ 是灯泡到第 $*i*$ 个发电机的欧几里得距离。因此，我们的任务是最小化![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f797f28d86c195134fb9568607febdc9ad9f7336.png)。当然，我们知道所有发电机的位置。

灯泡应当位于教室的天花板上。教室的天花板是一个严格凸的 $*m*$ 边形（教室本身是一个直棱柱，底面为严格凸的 $*m*$ 边形）。请帮助找出灯泡的最优位置。假设所有发电机都位于教室天花板所在的平面内。设该平面上建立了某个笛卡尔坐标系。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$ $(2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5})$ —— 发电机的数量。接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*x*_{*i*},*y*_{*i*}$，表示平面内第 $*i*$ 个发电机的坐标。保证没有两个发电机位于同一位置。

下一行包含一个整数 $*m*$ $(3 ≤ *m* ≤ 10^{5})$ —— 描述天花板的凸多边形的顶点数。接下来的 $*m*$ 行中，每行包含两个整数 $*p*_{*i*}, *q*_{*i*}$，表示多边形按顺时针顺序排列的第 $*i*$ 个点的坐标。保证该多边形严格凸。

所有坐标的绝对值不超过 $10^{6}$。

## 输出格式

输出一个实数 —— 发电机到灯泡最优位置的距离平方和的最小值。当答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 4}$ 时，答案将被视为正确。

## 说明

我们将严格凸多边形定义为满足以下性质的凸多边形：多边形的任意三个顶点都不在同一直线上。
